docs.doc_summary: This document provides a detailed technical specification of two core modules in a conversational AI platform: the State Engine and the Agent Orchestrator. It covers the architecture, API surface, processing and storage layers, tenant-specific configuration, and message processing flow of the State Engine, as well as the agent manifest system, trigger and priority resolution mechanisms, handoff management, and namespace enforcement in the Agent Orchestrator. The document emphasizes deterministic, rule-based logic for orchestration and state management, with clear boundaries for agent interaction and extensibility for multi-tenant environments.

relevance_hints.best_for: This document is best for queries about the internal design, API methods, and operational logic of the State Engine and Agent Orchestrator modules, including how session state is managed, how agents are triggered and orchestrated, and how multi-tenant configuration and storage are handled. It is also highly relevant for questions about agent manifest structure, trigger conditions, handoff processes, and technical decisions regarding state and agent management.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: This document does NOT cover the implementation details of individual agents, LLM prompt engineering, user interface design, external API integrations, or modules outside of the State Engine and Agent Orchestrator (such as Feedback Engine, RBAC, or Analytics Engine). It does not provide end-user documentation or deployment instructions.

top_sections.title: Module 1: State Engine
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the State Engine's purpose, API surface, processing and storage layers, tenant configuration, message processing flow, and the structure of the session state object, detailing how state is managed, validated, and persisted across the platform.

top_sections.title: Module 2: Agent Orchestrator
top_sections.section_summary: Explains the Agent Orchestrator's role in agent activation, priority resolution, handoff management, and enforcement of state write boundaries, focusing on deterministic, rule-based orchestration and agent lifecycle management.

top_sections.title: 1.1 API Surface
top_sections.section_summary: Details the five core API methods of the State Engine, including readState, writeState, subscribe, assembleContext, and queryHistory, with explanations of their usage, parameters, and impact on session state.

top_sections.title: 2.1 Agent Manifest System
top_sections.section_summary: Outlines the structure and consumption of agent manifests, the four agent types, and how manifests drive agent registration, triggering, context assembly, and execution within the orchestrator.

top_sections.title: 2.4 Handoff Manager
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the mechanisms for agent handoff, including confidence scoring, atomic handoff operations, auto-filling discovery dimensions, and preservation of agent-specific progress during workflow transitions.

docs.doc_summary: This document provides a comprehensive technical specification for Module 3: Knowledge Base Engine, the intelligence layer of a conversational AI platform. It details the architecture, ingestion, processing, classification, indexing, retrieval, and lifecycle management of both unstructured and structured knowledge, including the integration of Azure Foundry IQ and proprietary knowledge stores. The document emphasizes the design and operation of the product relationship graph, multi-source retrieval orchestration, caching strategies, and key technical decisions underpinning the system.
key_topics: Product relationship graph schema and traversal

relevance_hints.best_for: This document is best for queries about the internal design, data flow, and technical decisions of the Knowledge Base Engine, including ingestion, classification, retrieval, product relationship graph construction, and integration with Foundry IQ. It is highly relevant for understanding how knowledge is processed, stored, and retrieved for agentic use cases, as well as the rationale behind architectural choices and lifecycle management.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: This document does NOT cover the implementation details of the State Engine, Agent Orchestrator, user interface design, external API integrations, or modules outside of the Knowledge Base Engine (such as Feedback Engine, RBAC, or Analytics Engine). It does not provide end-user documentation, agent prompt engineering, or deployment instructions.

top_sections.title: 3.1 Ingestion Layer
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the fan-out ingestion pipeline, including file upload, deduplication, metadata cataloging, content classification, and integration with Foundry IQ for indexing and parsing. Emphasizes automation, tenant isolation, and supported file types.

top_sections.title: 3.2 Processing Pipeline
top_sections.section_summary: Covers the content classification process using LLMs, cross-KB intelligence extraction, intelligence routing to various stores, and chunking strategies for both unstructured and structured data.

top_sections.title: 3.3 KB Core — Knowledge Stores
top_sections.section_summary: Details the architecture of per-tenant knowledge stores, including the unified Foundry IQ semantic search layer and multiple structured PostgreSQL stores for products, relationships, competitors, customer patterns, and playbooks.

top_sections.title: 3.4 Product Relationship Graph
top_sections.section_summary: Explains the schema, relationship types, graph building strategy, confidence model, and traversal algorithms for the proprietary product relationship graph, which underpins intelligent recommendations.

top_sections.title: 3.5 Retrieval Layer — Multi-Source Query Orchestration
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the orchestration of parallel queries across multiple knowledge sources, agent-specific source mapping, and query construction strategies to maximize retrieval relevance for agentic tasks.

docs.doc_summary: This document provides a detailed technical specification for Module 4: Data Integration Layer of a data platform. It covers the architecture, connector framework, field mapping, data transformation and normalization, sync management, data routing to platform targets, outbound write-back processes, and the complete data pipeline flow. The document also addresses MVP CSV import flows, validation, risks, and key technical decisions for scalable and extensible data integration.

MVP CSV import flow and validation

It is highly relevant for understanding connector architecture, field mapping, data pipeline flow, error handling, and CSV import processes.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: This document does NOT cover the internal logic of the State Engine, Agent Orchestrator, Knowledge Base Engine, user interface design, agent prompt engineering, or modules outside of data integration. It does not provide end-user documentation, deployment instructions, or details on feedback, RBAC, or analytics modules.

top_sections.title: 4.2 Connector Framework
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the standardized connector architecture for integrating external systems, including connector types, authentication, interface contracts, and credential storage, with a roadmap for future CRM/API integrations.

top_sections.title: 4.3 Field Mapping Engine
top_sections.section_summary: Explains the field mapping process, canonical schema, and ML-based auto-suggest for mapping source data fields to platform-standard fields, ensuring schema consistency across integrations.

top_sections.title: 4.4 Transform & Normalize
top_sections.section_summary: Covers data transformation, normalization, deduplication, enrichment, and aggregation processes that standardize and enhance imported data for reliable downstream use.

top_sections.title: 4.5 Sync Manager
top_sections.section_summary: Details the management of data synchronization, including initial load, incremental sync, scheduling, and error handling with a dead letter queue to ensure robust and reliable data updates.

top_sections.title: 4.10 MVP Implementation — CSV Import Flow
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the MVP CSV import process, including supported import types, user experience, validation rules, and error handling for simple, reliable data onboarding.

docs.doc_summary: This document provides a comprehensive technical specification for Module 5, which defines the multi-tenancy and tenant configuration framework for a SaaS platform. It details strategies for tenant isolation, domain research and schema configuration, business rules engine, agent configuration, onboarding flows, and key technical decisions for supporting industry-specific adaptation and secure, flexible tenant management. The document contrasts MVP and full product approaches, emphasizing security, configurability, and operational best practices for onboarding and managing diverse B2B tenants.

Technical decisions for SaaS tenant management

It is highly relevant for understanding how the platform supports secure, flexible, and industry-specific tenant onboarding and management, including technical decisions and configuration strategies.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: This document does NOT cover the internal logic of the State Engine, Agent Orchestrator, Knowledge Base Engine, Data Integration Layer, user interface design outside of configuration UI, agent prompt engineering, or modules unrelated to tenant configuration and onboarding. top_sections.title: 5.1 Tenant Isolation Layer
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the strategy and enforcement mechanisms for strict tenant isolation, including row-level security with tenant_id, application middleware, PostgreSQL RLS, and resource-specific isolation methods to prevent cross-tenant data access.

top_sections.title: 5.2 Domain Research — How to Prepare for a New Industry
top_sections.section_summary: Outlines the framework for researching and documenting industry-specific requirements, including sales motion, product taxonomy, customer segmentation, and schema differences, to enable rapid and accurate tenant onboarding.

top_sections.title: 5.3 Configuration Framework
top_sections.section_summary: Details the architecture and storage of tenant configuration, including versioned JSONB schemas, caching strategies, and the evolution from manual JSON editing to a visual admin portal for configuration management.

top_sections.title: 5.4 Business Rules Engine
top_sections.section_summary: Explains the types, schema, enforcement timing, and onboarding process for tenant-specific business rules that guide recommendations, compliance, and sales strategies within the platform.

top_sections.title: 5.7 Onboarding Flow — Complete Deep Dive
top_sections.section_summary: Provides a detailed, step-by-step onboarding process, specifying required client data, handling of degraded states, and the use of industry templates to accelerate and standardize tenant setup.

docs.doc_summary: This document provides a detailed technical specification for Modules 6–11, which constitute the Core Agent Layer of a conversational AI sales platform. It covers the architecture, context assembly, data sourcing, trigger mechanisms, agent workflows, prompt engineering, business rules enforcement, and feedback-driven prompt evolution for agents handling Cross-Sell, Upsell, Full Solution, Renewal, Win-Back, and Net-New sales motions. The document emphasizes phase-aware output, agent-orchestrator communication, industry-neutral design with domain-specific adaptations, and robust safeguards for recommendation quality and system integrity.

relevance_hints.best_for: This document is best for queries about the internal logic, workflow, and technical design of sales-focused AI agents (Cross-Sell, Upsell, Full Solution, Renewal, Win-Back, Net-New), including how they assemble context, generate outputs, enforce business rules, and evolve prompts based on feedback. It is highly relevant for understanding agent phase transitions, prompt structure, data dependencies, and the interaction between agents and the orchestrator.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: This document does NOT cover the architecture or implementation of the State Engine, Agent Orchestrator, Knowledge Base Engine, Data Integration Layer, or tenant configuration modules. It does not provide end-user documentation, UI design, external API integration details, or deployment instructions.

top_sections.title: Modules 6–11: Core Agent Layer
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the overall architecture, responsibilities, and boundaries of the Core Agent Layer, detailing the roles of each agent type, their workflow phases, and the MVP versus post-MVP scope.

top_sections.title: 6.1 Context Assembly — How Each Agent Gets Different Context
top_sections.section_summary: Explains how each agent receives a tailored context package, with a comparative table showing context components, data sources, and token budgets for each agent type.

top_sections.title: 6.5 Conversation Stages and Phase-Aware Output
top_sections.section_summary: Details the three operational phases (discovery, recommendation, action) for agents, including structured output formats and how agent behavior and outputs change by phase.

top_sections.title: 6.7 Prompt Architecture
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the standardized prompt template, how business rules are injected and enforced, and how prompts are adapted for different industries and agent roles.

top_sections.title: 6.8 Prompt Versioning and Evolution
top_sections.section_summary: Covers prompt versioning ownership, schema, and the feedback-driven process for evolving prompts, including policies for manual, semi-automatic, and automatic updates.

top_sections.title: 12.1 SDK Architecture Overview
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the overall architecture of the Plugin Agent SDK, emphasizing its role as an interface contract and runtime sandbox within the platform, and explains the execution model managed by the Orchestrator and Plugin Gateway.

top_sections.title: 12.2 Security Model — Five Layers of Isolation
top_sections.section_summary: Details the five-layer security model for plugin execution, including sandboxed environments, scoped API access, state write restrictions, output sanitization, and review gates for custom plugins.

top_sections.title: 12.8 Built-In Quick Actions — All 8 Plugins
top_sections.section_summary: Specifies the eight built-in quick action plugins, detailing their triggers, data usage, output formats, LLM involvement, and deployment strategy within the platform.
